title: The Lion and the Mouse
style: Layered paper-craft illustration: cut paper collage with soft drop shadows between layers and visible paper fibre texture, warm muted palette (sage green, mustard yellow, terracotta, soft blue, cream), gentle children's storybook look. Vertical 9:16, 1080x1920. The top 22% is plain cream sky (only a paper sun and one small paper cloud) so a caption fits there. No text, no letters, no logos, no watermark. Every frame uses the same wide camera angle and the same layout: acacia tree on the left, hills in the back, sun top right.
characters: LION: big, friendly-looking male lion, mustard-gold paper body, layered terracotta-orange paper mane, small round ears, dark brown nose. MOUSE: tiny grey paper mouse with big round pink ears, thin pink tail, small black eyes. Same savanna setting in every frame: one wide acacia tree, tall pale-yellow grass, soft blue distant hills.

sentences.en: A big lion sleeps under a tree.
sentences.tr: Büyük bir aslan ağacın altında uyur.
sentences.scene: The lion sleeps peacefully under the acacia tree, eyes closed, head on his paws.

sentences.en: A little mouse runs on his paw.
sentences.tr: Küçük bir fare onun pençesinin üstünden koşar.
sentences.scene: Same wide view of the acacia tree: the lion sleeps under it, and the tiny mouse runs across the lion's big front paw.

sentences.en: The lion wakes up. He is angry!
sentences.scene: The lion is awake and angry, holding the mouse by the tail under one paw; the mouse looks scared.

sentences.en: “Please, let me go!” says the mouse.
sentences.scene: The tiny mouse, held under the paw, puts its little hands together and begs the big lion.
The mouse points to itself proudly while the lion raises an eyebrow, doubtful.

sentences.en: The lion laughs and lets him go.
sentences.scene: The lion laughs with his head back; the mouse runs away happily into the grass.

sentences.en: One day, the lion is in a net.
sentences.tr: Bir gün aslan bir ağa yakalanır.
sentences.scene: The lion is trapped in a big rope net under the acacia tree, looking worried.
The lion, still in the net, roars loudly with mouth wide open; paper birds fly away from the tree.
Same wide view: the lion is still trapped in the rope net under the acacia tree, roaring; far away in the tall grass the tiny mouse stops and lifts its big ears, listening.

sentences.en: Bite, bite, bite! He bites the net.
sentences.scene: Same wide view of the acacia tree: the lion sits in the rope net; the tiny mouse stands on the net and bites the ropes, some ropes already broken.
The lion stands free and happy, the broken net on the ground; the mouse stands next to his paw.

sentences.en: Little friends can be great friends.
sentences.scene: The lion and the mouse sit together under the acacia tree at sunset, the mouse on the lion's head, both smiling.
